declared_conflicts: the same session wrote this worked example's protocol after the run; it is an illustration of the record shapes, not an independent review

checks.detail: 5 files and every artifact hash recomputed from disk
export binds the frozen protocol; arms, seeds, row counts and isolation agree

A/A arm rho-neg-aa reproduces rho-neg row for row (identical S on all 6 measured pairs, identical algorithm_seed per (workload, round): True); under same seeds the A/A spread is 0 and measures determinism, not the walk's seed variance. The between-round spread of rho-neg itself (workload W141767324d6e: 2.029, 1.355, 1.079; W8d7a772f8ccd: 0.808, 0.864, 1.776) is the floor a method difference must exceed. The protocol's C-aa therefore does not deliver the noise floor it was written for: an A/A arm needs independent seeds. Positive and negative controls are excused in the protocol; the harness verified [k]G = Q on all 24 rows (24 verified).

Recomputed from export rows: sum S bsgs-neg 5.6244, sum S rho-neg 7.9112, ratio 0.7109; median S bsgs-neg 0.9374 vs rho-neg 1.2167; bsgs-neg S is constant per workload (1.108, 0.767), rho-neg varies by seed. Numbers agree with crypto:research/eks_crypto_validation_20261019 counts (72 verified records of which these 24 are the subset).

The decision rule asks for a paired bootstrap interval over workloads; with two workloads the interval degenerates and the A/A half-width is 0 under shared seeds, so the rule cannot be applied as written. No verdict on C2 beyond descriptive.

One registered 20-bit prime-order curve, two targets, three rounds, one binary (583e62f0), one Spot c8in.xlarge VM; every row L0, so no clock is evidence; nothing here is a scaling or speed claim, as the protocol's inadmissible list says.
Protocol declares no masking and the export's analysis.blinded is false, consistently; the arms are named by method in harness output.
All 18 measured rows wall_valid false (earned L0 < required L2; blockers: unmovable user thread, preflight not quiet, 104 preemptions/s); counted S and total_gae stand. 0 not_completed, 0 excluded.

replay.method: ecbench verify --dir session --replay K (not run: the crypto binary is not built in this checkout)

observations: rho-neg and rho-neg-aa rows are identical pair for pair (seeds equal: True); the A/A spread is 0.
bsgs-neg S is 1.108 on W141767324d6e and 0.767 on W8d7a772f8ccd in every round (deterministic given the target); ratio of summed S bsgs-neg/rho-neg = 0.7109.
Every row earned L0; the pod audit in crypto reproduced 54/54 measured replays; this review did not replay.
bsgs-neg carries inserts_uncharged and lookups_uncharged counters (376 and 441 on row ECR1h...); rho-neg carries canonicalisations_uncharged (674); the 0 / 0.1 / 1 GAE band was not applied here.

judgments.basis: 24/24 rows outcome verified; the harness recomputed [k]G = Q against the planted scalar on every row

descriptively bsgs-neg sums to 0.711x the reference S, below rho on this fixture, the opposite direction of P1; but the A/A arm shares seeds with the reference and the two-workload interval cannot be formed, so the decision rule does not apply as written
judgments.scope: one 20-bit curve, two targets, three rounds

open_questions: Does ecbench's control arm draw independent algorithm_seed values when same_seeds is not requested, or is the shared seed the spec's measurement.seed behaviour? The protocol must say which A/A it wants.
With the uncharged counters priced at 0.1 and 1 GAE on both arms, does the order of bsgs-neg and rho-neg hold?

recommendation.reason: amend the protocol so the A/A arm uses independent seeds and the sample has at least eight targets per curve, then rerun; this fixture validates the record shapes and nothing about the methods

asserts_nothing_about: any speed or scaling claim about rho or BSGS
